_meta.note: Definitions are drafts for review by qualified trichology/dermatology/cosmetic-science reviewers. Measurement methods list candidate approaches, not validated protocols.

terms.label: Hair fiber characteristics
terms.definition: Root concept grouping observable and measurable properties of the hair shaft.
terms.consumerDefinition: How your hair strands look, feel and behave.
terms.researchDefinition: Physical, chemical and geometric properties of the keratinized hair shaft.

terms.label: Curl geometry
terms.definition: Shape of the hair fiber along its length, including curl diameter, wave frequency and twist.
terms.consumerDefinition: How straight, wavy, curly or coily your hair is.
terms.researchDefinition: Curvature descriptors of the fiber (e.g. curl diameter, curve index, number of waves, twist frequency).
terms.measurementMethod: Self-report category; image-based curvature measurement; standardized curl-template comparison.

terms.label: Strand diameter
terms.definition: Cross-sectional width of an individual hair fiber.
terms.consumerDefinition: Whether individual strands are fine, medium or coarse.
terms.researchDefinition: Fiber diameter or cross-sectional area, noting ellipticity for non-circular fibers.
terms.measurementMethod: Micrometer or laser scan micrometry; optical microscopy; self-report category.

terms.label: Hair density
terms.definition: Number of hairs per unit area of scalp.
terms.consumerDefinition: How many strands you have — thin, medium or thick overall.
terms.researchDefinition: Hairs per cm² at defined scalp sites.

terms.label: Apparent porosity
terms.definition: Observed tendency of hair to absorb and release water, used as a proxy for cuticle condition.
terms.consumerDefinition: How quickly your hair soaks up water and dries.
terms.researchDefinition: Water uptake/release behavior; no single validated consumer test exists — 'float tests' are not validated.
terms.measurementMethod: Dynamic vapor sorption; water uptake by mass; self-report (low/medium/high/not sure).

terms.label: Elasticity
terms.definition: Ability of a hair fiber to stretch and return to its original length.
terms.consumerDefinition: Whether a strand stretches and bounces back, or snaps.
terms.researchDefinition: Extension and recovery behavior in the elastic region of the stress–strain curve.
terms.measurementMethod: Single-fiber tensile testing (wet/dry); self-report stretch test.

terms.label: Tensile behavior
terms.definition: Mechanical response of hair fibers to applied force, including break stress and strain.
terms.consumerDefinition: How strong strands are when pulled.
terms.researchDefinition: Young's modulus, break stress, break strain and work to break from single-fiber or bundle tests.

terms.label: Breakage
terms.definition: Fracture of hair fibers along the shaft, distinct from shedding at the root.
terms.consumerDefinition: Short broken pieces of hair, especially when combing or styling.
terms.researchDefinition: Count or mass of broken fiber fragments under a standardized grooming protocol, or self-reported frequency.
terms.measurementMethod: Combing breakage counts; fatigue cycles to failure; self-report frequency scale.

terms.label: Moisture retention
terms.definition: Ability of hair to retain water content over time after wetting or product application.
terms.consumerDefinition: How long hair feels moisturized after washing or styling.
terms.researchDefinition: Water content over time under controlled humidity.
terms.measurementMethod: Gravimetric water content; dynamic vapor sorption; self-report duration.

terms.label: Frizz response
terms.definition: Degree of fiber misalignment and volume expansion in response to humidity or friction.
terms.consumerDefinition: How puffy or flyaway hair becomes, especially in humid weather.
terms.researchDefinition: Image-derived frizz/volume metrics under controlled humidity; static charge measures.
terms.measurementMethod: Standardized imaging in humidity chamber; self-report scale.

terms.label: Shrinkage
terms.definition: Reduction in apparent length of curly or coily hair compared with its stretched length.
terms.consumerDefinition: How much shorter your hair looks than it really is.
terms.researchDefinition: Ratio of relaxed apparent length to stretched length.
terms.measurementMethod: Paired length measurement (stretched vs relaxed); image analysis.

terms.label: Length retention
terms.definition: Net change in hair length over time, reflecting growth minus breakage and trimming.
terms.consumerDefinition: Whether your hair is keeping its length over time.
terms.researchDefinition: Longitudinal length measurement at defined sites with trims recorded as confounders.

terms.label: Chemical damage
terms.definition: Alteration of hair structure from chemical processes such as relaxing, perming, bleaching or oxidative coloring.
terms.consumerDefinition: Damage from relaxers, perms, bleach or permanent color.
terms.researchDefinition: Changes in cystine/lanthionine content, protein loss, cuticle condition or tensile properties after chemical treatment.
terms.measurementMethod: Amino acid analysis; protein loss assays; SEM; self-reported service history.

terms.label: Heat damage
terms.definition: Structural change in hair from thermal styling.
terms.consumerDefinition: Damage from flat irons, blow-dryers or other hot tools — e.g. curls not returning.
terms.researchDefinition: Protein denaturation, cuticle damage or loss of curl recovery after thermal exposure.
terms.measurementMethod: DSC; SEM; curl-recovery testing; self-reported heat use.

terms.label: Mechanical damage
terms.definition: Damage from combing, brushing, tension, friction or styling manipulation.
terms.consumerDefinition: Damage from combing, tight styles or rough handling.
terms.researchDefinition: Cuticle lifting, fiber fracture or split ends attributable to mechanical stress.

terms.label: Color-treated hair
terms.definition: Hair that has undergone temporary, semi-permanent, permanent or bleaching color services.
terms.consumerDefinition: Hair you have dyed or lightened.
terms.researchDefinition: Exposure state: color service type, date and frequency.

terms.label: Protective-style exposure
terms.definition: Wearing of braids, twists, wigs, weaves, locs or similar styles, including duration and tension.
terms.consumerDefinition: Time spent in braids, twists, wigs, weaves or similar styles.
terms.researchDefinition: Style type, installation date, duration, perceived tension and removal method.

terms.label: Scalp condition
terms.definition: Root concept grouping visible and reported scalp characteristics.
terms.consumerDefinition: How your scalp looks and feels.
terms.researchDefinition: Cosmetic-level scalp observations; not diagnoses.

terms.label: Scalp dryness
terms.definition: Reported or observed tightness, dullness or dryness of the scalp skin.
terms.consumerDefinition: A tight or dry-feeling scalp.
terms.researchDefinition: Self-reported dryness; corneometry where measured.

terms.label: Scalp oiliness
terms.definition: Reported or measured sebum on the scalp surface.
terms.consumerDefinition: How quickly your scalp gets oily after washing.
terms.researchDefinition: Sebum casual level at a defined time after washing.

terms.label: Visible flaking
terms.definition: Visible scale or flakes on the scalp or hair.
terms.consumerDefinition: Flakes you can see on your scalp, hair or clothes.
terms.researchDefinition: Graded adherent/loose flaking at defined scalp sections (cosmetic grading — not a diagnosis of dandruff or dermatitis).
terms.measurementMethod: Standardized adherent scalp flaking score; image grading; self-report.

terms.label: Visible redness
terms.definition: Observed redness of scalp skin.
terms.consumerDefinition: Red areas on your scalp.
terms.researchDefinition: Erythema grading or image-derived redness index; cosmetic observation only.

terms.label: Buildup
terms.definition: Residue from products, sebum or minerals on scalp or hair.
terms.consumerDefinition: Coating or residue that makes hair feel heavy or scalp feel coated.
terms.researchDefinition: Residue deposition (e.g. polymer, silicone, mineral) measured or observed.

terms.label: Scalp sensitivity
terms.definition: Reported discomfort such as itching, burning or stinging.
terms.consumerDefinition: Itching, tingling, burning or tenderness on the scalp.
terms.researchDefinition: Self-reported sensory symptoms; irritation scores in controlled studies.

terms.label: Hairline observations
terms.definition: Observed changes at the frontal and temporal hairline, including at the edges.
terms.consumerDefinition: Changes you notice at your edges or hairline.
terms.researchDefinition: Standardized photographic comparison of hairline position and density; observation only, not a diagnosis.

terms.label: Apparent density change
terms.definition: Observed change in how full the hair appears over time.
terms.consumerDefinition: Whether your hair looks fuller or thinner than before.
terms.researchDefinition: Change in global photographic assessment or hair count; cosmetic appearance only. Clinical hair-loss conditions require medical evaluation.
